title: finding(tests): two Storage.prototype spy instruments carry no counter-probe — the bootSplash one injects a fault that never reaches the code, on Node 22 today
body:
Found while running the census #7271 asked for ("which other localStorage-instrumented
suites share the sensitivity"). The environment repair for that card is PR #7785; this is
the part of the census it deliberately does **not** repair, because the fix is a different
one (add counter-probes) in two packages that card does not reach.

Four suites instrument `Storage.prototype` directly:

```
apps/console/src/__tests__/bootSplash.test.ts
packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/anonSeedScope-5746.enumeration.test.tsx
packages/i18n/src/__tests__/provider-locale-persistence.test.tsx        (false positive — it says in a comment that it deliberately does NOT spy on the prototype)
packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/UserFilters.addTab.test.tsx
```

Only `anonSeedScope-5746` carries a counter-probe. It is the only one of the four that
went red when the instrument went blind. The other two real ones stayed **green** while
the instrument was proven blind in the same run — which is the failure mode #7271 was
filed about, arriving without a single failing assertion to announce it.

## 1. `apps/console/src/__tests__/bootSplash.test.ts` — the injected fault never lands

`it('survives a browser with no localStorage access')` installs

```ts
vi.spyOn(Storage.prototype, 'getItem').mockImplementation(() => { throw new Error('storage blocked'); });
```

and then asserts that `runBootSplash()` does not throw. **Measured:** with that spy
installed, a direct `localStorage.getItem('…')` in the same test, in the same tick, does
**not** throw — on Node **22.22.2** as well as 26.7.0, on a fully repaired tree. So the
"no localStorage access" condition is never simulated; the test asserts that a normal boot
does not throw, under a name that promises something else. This one is live today, on the
Node version CI pins.

Mechanism, measured in that project: `localStorage` has no own properties, and
`localStorage.getItem` is neither the patched prototype method nor the pre-patch one — it
is a third function object, i.e. happy-dom hands out a bound method through its Storage
proxy. A prototype patch installed after the store's method has first been reached is
invisible to it. (The same proxy behaviour, exercised deliberately, is what ablation E1 in
PR #7785 uses to blind `anonSeedScope-5746` on purpose.)

## 2. `packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/UserFilters.addTab.test.tsx` — a negative assertion with no liveness check

The load-bearing line is

```ts
expect(setItem).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(0);
```

on a `Storage.prototype` spy — a **negative** assertion, which a blind instrument
satisfies for the wrong reason. **Measured:** on Node 26.7.0 before the PR #7785 repair,
this file passed while the instrument was demonstrably blind; appending
`sessionStorage.setItem('probe','1'); expect(setItem).toHaveBeenCalled();` to the same
test made it fail there, and pass on the repaired tree. So the instrument is live again
once PR #7785 lands — but the file still has nothing that would tell anyone the next time
it is not.

## Why file it rather than widen that PR

PR #7785 removes today's exposure by repairing the shared environment, and its own suite
keeps its counter-probe. What it cannot do is give these two files the property that made
`anonSeedScope-5746` detect the problem in the first place. Case 1 in particular is a
present-day defect independent of any Node version, in a third package.

Suggested shape, not a decision: each `Storage.prototype`-spy suite asserts once that its
spy observes a write it makes itself, before it asserts anything about writes it did not
make. That is what the counter-probe in `anonSeedScope-5746` is.

Measured on objectui `aac3322e0`, Node 22.22.2 and Node 26.7.0.
